title: Semantic Knowledge Base Retrieval
business: Technical support teams managing large repositories of unstructured product documentation.
problem: Support agents struggle to find relevant troubleshooting steps when users describe issues using non-standard terminology or synonyms, leading to high resolution times.
solution: By utilizing all-mpnet-base-v2, the system transforms both user queries and documentation passages into dense vector embeddings. This allows the retrieval engine to identify semantically related passages even when exact keyword matches are absent, surfacing the correct documentation based on intent rather than literal phrasing.
steps: Pre-process the existing documentation library into discrete, manageable text chunks.
Use all-mpnet-base-v2 to generate vector embeddings for every document chunk.
Store these embeddings in a vector database to enable efficient similarity searches.
Convert incoming support queries into embeddings using the same model.
Perform a cosine similarity search to retrieve the most relevant documentation passages for the agent.
outcome: Support agents achieve faster access to accurate technical guidance, improving overall response consistency and reducing the cognitive load of searching through manual documentation.
limitation: The model has a fixed maximum sequence length; very long documents may be truncated, leading to information loss. This is checked by monitoring the token count of input passages before embedding generation.
